description: A side-by-side benchmark of a tree-walking interpreter and a bytecode VM, both running the same fibonacci program to show the speedup from compiling to bytecode.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: The only import is `time` for the `perf_counter` measurements.

`TreeWalker` evaluates AST nodes directly using an environment dict and match: literals return values, `Name` looks up env, and `Assign` evaluates and stores values. `BinOp` evaluates both sides and applies a dictionary lambda; `If` walks the chosen branch; `FunDecl` captures current env in a closure and stores a callable. `Call` evaluates callee and args then calls the function; `Return` raises custom `_Return` with the value to unwind the stack.
The bytecode side mirrors the earlier example: `Opcode` enum, `Instruction`, and `Chunk` with `emit`, `patch`, and `__len__`.
`_OPS2` maps operator strings to `Opcode` values for the compiler.

`Compiler2` matches statements: numbers emit `PUSH_INT`/`PUSH_FLOAT`; names emit `LOAD_NAME`; assignments compile value then `STORE_NAME`; binary ops compile both sides then mapped opcode. `if` compiles condition, `JUMP_IF_FALSE` over then, `JUMP` over else, and patches both; `FunDecl` creates inner compiler, emits reversed-param `STORE_LOCAL`, compiles body, emits `PUSH_NIL`/`RETURN`, then `MAKE_FUNCTION`/`STORE_NAME`. `Call` compiles callee and args then `CALL`; `Return` compiles value and `RETURN`.
`CallFrame2` holds chunk, ip, locals. `Function2` holds name, params, chunk. Frame `read` returns next instruction or `None`.

`VM2` has stack, frames, globals; `_execute` reads instructions: constants push, arithmetic pops two and pushes result, `LE` compares, `LOAD_NAME` checks locals then globals. `STORE_NAME` writes both; `LOAD_LOCAL`/`STORE_LOCAL` use frame locals; jumps move ip; `MAKE_FUNCTION` pushes `Function2`; `CALL` pops args and function, pushes reversed args for `STORE_LOCAL`, then new frame. `RETURN` pops frame and pushes return value; unimplemented opcodes are silently skipped.
`fib_ast` builds the same fibonacci function as before: a `FunDecl` with an `If` for the base case and a recursive `Return` of two `Call`s.

steps.answer: The bytecode VM is faster, typically 10x or more, because it avoids the overhead of traversing the AST nodes on every recursive call. The output prints both matching results for fib(22), their times in milliseconds, and the speedup ratio.
steps.question: The test runs both interpreters on `fib(22)`. The tree-walker evaluates the AST directly; the bytecode VM compiles to chunks and runs them. Which is faster and by how much?

title: Tree-Walker vs Bytecode VM Performance
